newsitem.title: USA: Miami police probe new killing, Versace cremated.
newsitem.headline: Miami police probe new killing, Versace cremated.

text.p: A wealthy doctor was murdered in Miami on Thursday and the FBI was probing the crime to see if alleged serial killer Andrew Cunanan, suspected of murdering designer Gianni Versace, had struck again.
As the manhunt for Cunanan ground on, Versace's relatives prepared to take his ashes home to Italy following the cremation of his body.

FBI and Miami police rushed to a house in Miami Springs, just north of the city's international airport, after a 44-year-old doctor was found murdered in his bed. A man fitting Cunanan's description was seen running from the house, police said.

"The description is pretty close (to Cunanan), the FBI is interested," Nelda Fonticiella, a Metro-Dade police spokeswoman, said. A neighbour saw a "white male, slim build, well dressed ... running from the scene."
Police said they had not established a definite link between the two murders. The dead doctor, named by one TV station as Silvio Alfonso, had been shot.
Local television stations quoted neighbours as saying the dead man was homosexual.

Police have called Cunanan a male prostitute while others who have studied his life before he began what authorities suspect was a spree of at least four murders say he was an upwardly mobile gigolo who preyed on wealthy gay men.
He also has been described as highly intelligent and a master of disguise.
Versace was shot and killed execution-style at the gates of his sumptuous Miami Beach mansion on Tuesday. Police have said Cunanan is their only suspect.
Earlier on Thursday, a funeral home source told Reuters that Versace "has been cremated and his ashes have been released to the family ... They are taking a private plane from Miami this morning."
The source, who declined to be identified, said Versace's body had been taken from the Riverside-Gordon Memorial Chapel in North Miami Beach and cremated in nearby Fort Lauderdale.
Versace's sister Donatella and brother Santo visited the Miami Beach mansion on Wednesday and were expected to travel back to Italy with the ashes.
A memorial service organised by the Italy-America Chamber of Commerce and Miami authorities was scheduled to be held on Friday at St. Patrick's Roman Catholic Church in Miami Beach.
In Washington, Attorney General Janet Reno said the FBI was doing everything it could to catch Cunanan and pledged to "make sure that we leave no stone unturned."

Justice Department officials said federal prosecutors in New Jersey late on Wednesday formally charged Cunanan with the May 9 shooting death of William Reese, a caretaker at a national cemetery in Pennsville, N.J.
FBI agent Paul Murray said in court documents that Reese's red Chevrolet pick-up truck was missing from the cemetery. It later was found parked near Versace's mansion in Miami Beach.
"A search of the truck revealed, among other things, a Bank of America check bearing the imprinted name of the defendant Cunanan as well as a passport in the defendant's name," Murray said.
In Miami, police and FBI agents scoured the city, questioning people on the street, in gay bars, hotels, restaurants and nightclubs.
Cunanan, 27, was already on the FBI's 10 Most Wanted list before the Versace killing because of four murders in three states in April and May.
Miami gays said they feared he was still in their midst.
Danilo de la Torre, an actor who performs as a drag queen in South Beach clubs, said his show was nearly empty on Tuesday night as customers stayed home to watch news about the murder.
"People are shocked it could happen, really shocked and scared. He's still out there," de la Torre said.
Police said they did not know if Versace, a homosexual, had any relationship with Cunanan, although Vanity Fair writer Maureen Orth said the two men had met at least once in San Francisco.
The San Francisco Chronicle reported on Thursday that the two men may have met in October 1990 when the designer was in San Francisco creating costumes for the city Opera.
